properties.name: Balkans Zone
properties.principle: Culture and history: the Balkans as Starcom counts them, nine states whole (Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Greece, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia), the name's common meaning in news, aid and policy, rather than the physical peninsula south of the Kupa–Sava–Danube line. Its Sectors follow the land's own lines: the Adriatic–Black Sea watershed, the Kupa, Sava and Drina, the ridges round the Kosovo basin, the Šar's foot, the Pindus, Olympus, the Strymon and the sea between the mainland and the islands; where a range or river is a border, the line is that border as Natural Earth draws it. No Sector names a state or says who a territory belongs to.

declared.name: Islets under 20 km2
declared.note: 23 small parts of the outline (205.45 km2 in all, islets in Natural Earth's polygons) are left out to keep the document within Starcom's vertex limits; no Sector covers them.

declared.name: Rim crossings at the Ibar and the Binačka Morava
declared.note: The Kosovo basin's rim is drawn along ridgelines (the Prokletije, Hajla, Mokra Gora, Rogozna, Kopaonik, the Goljak and the Skopska Crna Gora), and twice across a valley with no ridge to follow: the Ibar at its confluence with the Raška, between Rogozna and Kopaonik, and the Binačka Morava east of Gjilan, between the Goljak and the Karadak. Both crossings are drawn straight by judgement. The rim neither follows nor stands for the line between Kosovo and Serbia, whose status is disputed: the Sector takes in Serbian land north of it (the Ibar gorge to Raška, Kopaonik's crest) and North Macedonian land to the south (the Šar's southern slopes).

properties.name: Adriatic Coast and Dinaric Karst
properties.character: The Dinarides' Adriatic side: Istria, the Kvarner and the Dalmatian islands and coast, the karst uplands of Lika and Herzegovina on the Neretva, and Montenegro's coast and karst to Lake Skadar.
